findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true while sitting in a VPC, so the MySQL endpoint (admin user, port 3306) receives a public IP and is reachable from the internet if the security group permits it. The instance is also passed to user_data of an EC2 instance, exposing the endpoint further.
storage_encrypted = false leaves the database's underlying EBS volumes and any snapshots unencrypted, so anyone with access to the storage layer can read the catalog data in cleartext.

The master username is the well-known default 'admin' with no rotation and the password is supplied via var.password and then embedded into EC2 user_data, so credentials for a publicly accessible admin account are predictable and broadly exposed.

The instance user_data writes the RDS endpoint, username, and the plaintext database password (var.password) into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc via a shell heredoc. User data is retrievable from instance metadata by any process/user on the host and is stored in Terraform state and the AWS console, leaking DB credentials.

MySQL port 3306 is opened to the entire VPC CIDR block (aws_vpc.portal_vpc.cidr_block) rather than a specific application security group, so any host in the VPC, including compromised or unrelated instances, can connect to the database.

The instance role grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", giving the web server full control over all S3 buckets, EC2 resources, and RDS databases in the account. A compromise of this instance permits complete account takeover and data destruction.

The database security group allows all outbound traffic to 0.0.0.0/0 on all ports and protocols, enabling data exfiltration and outbound command-and-control from the DB tier if the instance is compromised.

monitoring_interval = 0 and backup_retention_period = 0 disable enhanced monitoring and automated backups, removing the ability to detect or recover from unauthorized access to the database. Note: reported only as it removes a compensating control for the exposed DB.

The user_data installs and starts Apache serving the catalog page over plain HTTP with no TLS or authentication; combined with the reported public DNS output and the broad security group, the application and its DB-fetching logic are reachable in cleartext.
